Ask around town what Bakersfield runs on and you will hear two answers, oil and agriculture, often from the same person. Good Bakersfield website design starts there. A machine shop off Rosedale Highway may rebuild a pump one week and a harvester part the next, and a staffing firm may fill rig crews and packing shifts in the same month. The site has to speak to both kinds of buyer without confusing either.

Maurice Johnson writes every page by hand and shows you a free demo before you pay. The prices are on the page: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time.

Web design in Bakersfield for the two economies

The oil side

Kern County has long produced most of California's crude; The Guardian reported in 2021 that Kern produced about 70% of the state's oil. In September 2025 the governor signed SB 237, a law meant to speed new well permits in Kern County. Operators, service companies, inspectors and the shops that keep their equipment running all need sites that show capability and safety, not slogans.

The farm side

Kern's 2024 crop report totaled about $7.96 billion, down from a record $8.63 billion in 2023, the year Kern ranked as the top farm county in the country. Citrus led at $1.31 billion, then grapes at $1.18 billion and carrots at $1.01 billion, with almonds near $800 million. Growers, packers, haulers, labor contractors and irrigation crews make up a second business community that buys very differently from the first.

Trades that sell to both sides, and what their sites need

  • Welding and fabrication. Separate pages for field repair and shop work, the materials you weld and whether you send a rig out to the lease or the ranch.
  • Electrical and pump service. Well pumps, motors and panels for growers on one page, wellsite and facility work on another, each with your license details stated plainly.
  • Trucking and equipment hauling. Trailer types, lanes and what you can and cannot move, plus a short quote form that asks for pickup, drop and dates.
  • Staffing and safety training. Which roles you fill or which courses you teach, who they suit, and how a company or a worker gets started.

In every case the buyer is busy and reading on a phone. The first screen should say what you do and where, and the call button should work with one thumb.

A music town with honky-tonk roots

Bakersfield also gave its name to a sound. The Bakersfield sound grew up as a rougher answer to polished Nashville records, built on live musicianship, honky-tonk rhythm and a touch of rock and roll, and Buck Owens and Merle Haggard carried it onto the national charts. Owens opened the Crystal Palace in 1996 as a nightclub and a museum of country music; in August 2025 the Owens family announced that it would close and said it hoped a new owner would carry it on.

For restaurants, bars and event spaces that book live music, that history is a reason to keep a calendar page current. A show list that is three months stale tells people you may not be open at all.

Bakersfield website design that names the right side of town

The Census Bureau estimated Bakersfield at 417,468 people in July 2024, and the city is spread out. Oildale sits in North Bakersfield between Highway 99 and the Kern River. Seven Oaks and Stockdale are in the southwest. Rosedale Highway is one of the main east and west roads through the northwest, with shopping centers along it. Downtown has its own mix of offices, restaurants and older storefronts.

Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence. A plumber in the southwest and a feed store in Oildale are reaching different neighbors, so each site should say where the business is and how far it travels, in the words residents use.

Web design services in Bakersfield, priced plainly

Starter is $497 for five hand-written pages (home, services, about, contact, service area), a contact form that emails every lead, Google Maps and hours, and titles and a sitemap submitted to Google, live in 7 to 14 days. Pro is $997 and adds a 10-page site with a gallery, Google Business Profile setup, schema markup, ten researched city pages and an AI chat widget, free for 14 days and then $297 a month if you keep it. Agency is $1,997 and adds keyword research across your area and a page for each worthwhile town and service, delivered in waves with the first live inside two weeks, plus AI phone agent setup; the agent is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time. Hosting, maintenance and updates run $49 a month, or are included in the $297 monthly fee while you keep an AI agent. We do not sell page counts. Ten useful pages beat forty thin ones.

Local help worth calling first

The CSUB Small Business Development Center at California State University, Bakersfield gives free one-on-one consulting to owners and would-be owners in Kern, Inyo and Mono counties, covering starting, managing and financing a business, and runs free webinars. The Greater Bakersfield Chamber of Commerce offers networking, a 401(k) multiple employer plan for small employers and labor law help; CalChamber gave it an HR Champion Award in 2023 for helping members follow California employment law.

Common questions

How much does web design in Bakersfield, CA cost?

Local quotes swing from a few hundred dollars to several thousand, and some carry a monthly fee for as long as the site exists. Ours are fixed and paid once: Starter $497, Pro $997, Agency $1,997. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month. If you keep one of our AI agents after its free trial, it is $297 a month and hosting is included. Ask every web design company in Bakersfield you talk to for the first-year total in writing.

How often should a business website be redesigned?

There is no fixed calendar. Redesign when the site stops matching the business: you added or dropped a service, it is hard to read on a phone, it loads slowly, or you cannot change your own hours without calling someone. Small updates should happen all the time, and they are part of our maintenance. A full rebuild only makes sense when the structure itself is in the way.

Can one website serve both oilfield and farm customers?

Yes, if each group gets its own page. A welding or electrical shop that works both sides should have one page written for operators and service companies and another for growers and packers, each with the work, the equipment and the safety or food safety details that buyer cares about.

Do you have an office in Bakersfield?

No. Maurice Johnson builds every site remotely from Big Sandy in East Texas. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
